In re: An application under Article 226 of the  Constitution of India;
 And  Bidyut Chakraborty  -versus-  The State of West Bengal & ors.
 Mr. Apurba Ghosh,
 Mr. Souvik Das  ....for the Petitioner  Mr. Debabrata Chatterjee,
 Ms. Amrita Panja Moulick  ...for the State  Affidavit of service filed by the petitioner be kept on  record.
Mr. Das, learned advocate appearing for the  petitioner
submits that the petitioner, namely, Bidyut  Chakraborty (in short, Bidyut) married Rimpa  Chakraborty (in short, Rimpa).
They were blessed with a  male child, who is presently aged about 7 years.
They  were peacefully residing at the address given in the cause  title.
He further submits that Rimpa went missing on and  from 9th October, 2023.
Such fact was intimated to the  local police Station but no steps were taken.
As such the  petitioner submitted a further representation to the police  authorities on 10th October, 2023 but in vain.
Aggrieved  by such inaction on the part of the police authorities  Bidyut has approached this Court.

sentences.text: Ms. Panja Moulick, learned advocate appearing for  the State respondents
denies the contention of Mr. Das and submits that there was a matrimonial dispute between Bidyut and Rimpa.

Alleging that she had been tortured and had been driven out of her matrimonial house, Rimpa lodged a complaint which was registered as Galsi Police Station Case No.610 of 2023 dated 09 th October, 2023 under Sections 498A/406 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: Galsi Police Station Case No.610 of 2023
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In course of investigation, it was found that Rimpa was residing along with her child in a rented flat at Ghatak Building, Galsi Bazar, Police Staiton Galsi, District Burdwan.

Let the written instruction,
as produced, be kept on record.
Heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and considered the materials on record.
We do not find any material on record to infer any illegal detention.
Rimpa, an adult lady, is residing along with her child at the place mentioned hereinabove.
In view thereof, no further interference is called for in the present habeas corpus petition being WPA (H) 71 of 2023 and the same is dismissed.
There shall, however, be no order as to costs.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, be given to the learned advocates for the parties.

(Siddhartha Roy Chowdhury, J.) (Tapabrata Chakraborty, J.)
